chunks: And God fulfilled His promise to you when you were destroying them by His permission, until you were unmanned and disputed the order, and thus disobeyed (the Apostle) even after He had brought you in sight of (victory) you longed for. Some of you desired this world, and some of you the next. Then He put you to flight before (them) in order to try you. But (now) He has forgiven you, for surely God is kind to the faithful.
ai.seo_question: What happened to the Muslims at the Battle of Uhud according to the Quran?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Al Imran (3:152) reflects on the Battle of Uhud, where initial divine promise of victory was contingent upon obedience, but internal discord and desire for worldly spoils led to a tactical reversal. Shia scholarship emphasizes this as a pivotal test of the believers' resolve, highlighting the transition from collective success to individual accountability due to the split between those prioritizing dunya and those seeking akhirah. The verse concludes with divine grace, noting that despite the disobedience, God pardoned the community, underscoring His mercy toward the faithful.
